Curator Account Lifecycle Management (Curator PWA + Developer Interface)
Restricted Developer Interface & AR Asset Deployment Workflow
Three Audiences Implemented via Next.js Route Groups

nodes.label: Progressive Web Application and Service Worker Technology
nodes.norm_label: progressive web application and service worker technology

nodes.label: Offline: IndexedDB via Dexie + Workbox Service Worker
nodes.norm_label: offline: indexeddb via dexie + workbox service worker

nodes.label: Next.js 16 Breaking-Changes Docs Rule
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16.3.2 has breaking changes vs. training data; agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is auto-regenerated by `next dev`, so removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change - committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: BR-10 Public Approval
nodes.rationale: Only curator-approved info may ever reach the public site/Gallery/FAQ/QR/AR - prevents unvetted specimen data from leaking to the public-facing platform.

nodes.label: BR-11 Storage Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Detailed storage locations never appear outside authenticated curator functions - protects specimen security and prevents theft/exposure risk.

nodes.label: BR-12 Developer Restriction
nodes.rationale: Developer role is strictly limited to onboarding/access-admin + AR asset deploy and is distinct from curator - keeps the developer interface from becoming a general-purpose admin dashboard.

nodes.label: BR-16 Offline Position
nodes.rationale: Offline = read-only cache + new Uncataloged drafts only; never offline edits to existing records - deliberately avoids building an online/offline conflict-resolution engine.

nodes.label: BR-18 FAQ Boundary
nodes.rationale: FAQ assistant is rule-based against curator-approved content only; unmatched queries fall back to the General Inquiry form - prevents unrestricted/generative chatbot behavior.

nodes.label: BR-21/22 Outbound Email Boundary
nodes.rationale: BioSphere sends email but never connects to/reads an external mailbox - avoids external mailbox sync complexity and the security exposure of reading Gmail/Outlook replies.

nodes.label: Single-Repo, Three-Audience Decision
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-08-27: serve the public website, curator PWA, and restricted developer interface from one Next.js app using route groups, rather than the two separate frontends called for in the SRS - keeps BioSphere to exactly two repos total (this frontend + a separate NestJS backend).

nodes.label: Two-Layer Auth Checking
nodes.rationale: Both proxy.ts and verifySession() are needed - neither alone is sufficient - because proxy matchers can drift out of sync with real routes, so the real check must be re-run inside every Server Action/data call.

nodes.label: BR-12: Developer Restriction
nodes.rationale: Developer role is not a curator role; strictly limited to curator onboarding/access-admin and approved AR asset deployment, never a general admin dashboard.

nodes.label: Edit User Modal (Developer)
nodes.rationale: Developer can update authorized curator account details/status when formally authorized but cannot view or assign passwords; password setup and recovery are completed only through secure email links, keeping credential control outside the developer role.

nodes.label: Section 3.1.4: Restricted Developer Interface
nodes.rationale: Developer interface must be minimal and not reproduce the curator application; limited to curator account onboarding/activation/disabling/removal and approved AR asset deployment, with all actions authenticated and audited. Routine specimen, location, request, report, FAQ, and public-content functions are not visible or accessible to the developer role.

nodes.label: BR-10: Public Approval
nodes.rationale: Only curator-approved information may ever reach the public site, Gallery, FAQ, QR pages, or AR content.

nodes.label: BR-11: Storage Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Detailed storage locations never appear outside authenticated curator functions.

nodes.label: BR-18: FAQ Boundary
nodes.rationale: FAQ assistant is rule-based against curator-approved content only; unmatched questions fall back to the General Inquiry form rather than generating an answer.

nodes.label: Section 3.1.6: Controlled Knowledge-Based FAQ Assistant Interface
nodes.norm_label: section 3.1.6: controlled knowledge-based faq assistant interface
nodes.rationale: The FAQ assistant widget must present a clear museum-assistant identity, suggested questions, and a visible path to the General Inquiry form; it must disclose that answers are limited to curator-approved museum knowledge and must not appear to approve visits or process campus entry, preventing visitor confusion about its authority.

nodes.label: Section 3.1.5: Public QR Exhibit Interfaces
nodes.rationale: QR exhibit pages must be mobile-optimized and show only approved images/educational content; internal fields, condition notes, storage locations, audit information, and curator-only remarks must never appear, keeping the public surface strictly limited to curator-approved and non-confidential data.

nodes.label: QR Exhibit Page (With View in AR Action)
nodes.norm_label: qr exhibit page (with view in ar action)

nodes.label: Camera Permission Request Policy
nodes.rationale: Camera permission shall be requested only after a visitor explicitly starts an AR or scanning action, minimizing unnecessary access requests and respecting visitor privacy/consent expectations.
